# Switch

Switch presents one boolean setting as a native on/off control.

## Complete example

Declare a boolean property on the native component, then bind it with `native:model`:

```php
<?php

namespace App\NativeComponents;

use Illuminate\View\View;
use FirstlightUI\NativeComponent;

class NotificationSettings extends NativeComponent
{
    public bool $notifications = false;

    public function render(): View
    {
        return view('native.notification-settings');
    }
}
```

```blade
<firstlight:switch
    native:model="notifications"
    label="Notifications"
    helper="Receive account updates."
    a11y-hint="Controls notification delivery"
/>
```

## Props

| API | Accepted type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `bool` | Accepted value. Defaults to `false` when omitted. |
| `native:model` | a boolean component property | Synchronises the accepted boolean value through NativePHP. `native:model.live` is also accepted. |
| `label` | `string` | Visible setting label. |
| `helper` | `string` | Supporting text below the setting. |
| `error` | `string` | Error text and error semantics; shown instead of `helper` when non-empty. |
| `disabled` | `bool` | Prevents interaction and change events. |
| `a11y-label` | `string` | Explicit accessibility label when a visible label is inappropriate. |
| `a11y-hint` | `string` | Additional VoiceOver and TalkBack guidance. |
| `class` | `string` | External EDGE layout utilities. |

## Events

`@change` receives the proposed boolean value. Use it when the server decides whether to accept a change:

```php
public bool $notifications = false;

public function updateNotifications(bool $value): void
{
    $this->notifications = $value;
}
```

```blade
<firstlight:switch
    :value="$notifications"
    @change="updateNotifications"
    label="Notifications"
/>
```

`native:model` normally supplies the same callback for property synchronisation.

## Accepted values

Switch accepts only strict PHP booleans: `true` and `false`. Bind a literal Boolean with `:`:

```blade
<firstlight:switch :value="false" label="Notifications" />
```

`value="false"` is invalid because Blade passes it as a string. `null`, integers, string booleans, arrays, and objects are also rejected.

## State timing

Host the control in `FirstlightUI\NativeComponent` so unchanged full responses
receive the [response revision](../reference/compatibility.md#runtime-response-contract).

Switch is [server-authoritative](../concepts/server-authoritative-state.md). A native interaction immediately emits its proposed Boolean, but the visible on/off state remains the last value published by PHP. A response that accepts the proposal changes the visible state; a response that rejects it leaves the visible state unchanged. Every server publication clears a pending proposal, including one that republishes the same value. Programmatic publications update the accepted state without emitting `@change`.

Use `native:model` or `native:model.live`. Deferred `blur`, `lazy`, and `debounce` sync modes are rejected.

## Disabled behaviour

When `disabled` is `true`, Switch stays visible with its accepted on/off state and cannot emit a proposal or `@change` event.

## Accessibility

Provide a visible `label` or an explicit `a11y-label`; Firstlight warns during development when both are blank. The native controls expose the setting name, on/off value, disabled state, optional hint, and error semantics. SwiftUI provides a minimum 44-point target; the Material 3 row provides a minimum 48-dp target and one TalkBack switch focus stop.

## Validation and failure behaviour

Contract exceptions still reject non-Boolean values, unsupported `required` or
`placement`, and deferred sync modes before publication. User validation is
separate: screens that `use ValidatesFields` auto-bind the first MessageBag
message for the field's `native:model` or `error-for` name. An authored
`error` wins. See [Validate fields](../how-to/validate-fields.md). An error
takes precedence over helper text and is included in accessibility semantics.

## Platform behaviour

iOS uses a genuine SwiftUI `Toggle` with the native switch style and system motion. Android uses a genuine Material 3 `Switch` inside a row-owned switch semantic target, preserving Material state layers and TalkBack behaviour. The public EDGE API and server-authoritative state contract are shared; native geometry, presentation, and interaction remain platform-specific.

## Compatibility

Switch supports the versions listed in the current [compatibility reference](../reference/compatibility.md) and requires both native renderers to be compiled into the host application.

## Screenshots

| Platform | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | ![Switch on iOS in light mode](../screenshots/switch/ios-light.png) | ![Switch on iOS in dark mode](../screenshots/switch/ios-dark.png) |
| Android | ![Switch on Android in light mode](../screenshots/switch/android-light.png) | ![Switch on Android in dark mode](../screenshots/switch/android-dark.png) |

--- Source: docs/reference/validates-fields.md ---

# ValidatesFields

`FirstlightUI\Concerns\ValidatesFields` is a Livewire-shaped Laravel Validator
layer for NativePHP EDGE screens. `FirstlightUI\NativeComponent` includes the
trait. See [Validate fields](../how-to/validate-fields.md) for a complete
working screen.

Do not place `@nativeError` next to Firstlight fields. That directive emits a
sibling text node and skips native field error colour, helper replacement, and
accessibility.

## Methods

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `validate($rules = null, $messages = [], $attributes = [])` | Validates public properties. Returns the validated array. On failure, stores the exception bag and rethrows `ValidationException`. On success, clears messages for the validated keys. |
| `validateOnly($field, $rules = null, $messages = [], $attributes = [])` | Validates one key. On failure, replaces only that key. On success, forgets that key. Other bag keys stay put. |
| `addError($field, $message)` | Appends one message without throwing. |
| `resetValidation($field = null)` | Forgets one key, an array of keys, or the whole bag. |
| `getErrorBag()` | Returns the current `Illuminate\Support\MessageBag`. |
| `hasError($field)` | Whether that key currently has messages. |

`$rules` may be an array, `null` (use the screen's rules), or a class name.
A class name is resolved through the container when possible, then
`$source->rules()`, and optionally `messages()` and `attributes()`. This is
the Form Request path: Firstlight does not perform an HTTP redirect.

When `$messages` or `$attributes` are empty, the trait reads the screen's
`messages()` / `$messages` and `validationAttributes()` /
`$validationAttributes`.

Action dispatch catches `ValidationException` from `@press`, `@change`,
`@submit`, and `updated{Property}` handlers, stores the bag, and republishes
the screen. Other exceptions still propagate.

## Field binding

During the screen's view pass, participating fields read the current bag and
set their native `error` slot from the first message for the resolved name:

1. A non-empty authored `error` attribute wins and skips the bag.
2. Otherwise `error-for` (or `errorFor`) selects the bag key.
3. Otherwise the `native:model` / `native:model.*` property name is used.
4. Otherwise a compiled `__syncProperty('name')` change callback is used.

An empty authored `error` is treated as unset. Fields without a resolvable
name stay empty. Only the first message for a key is published.

The view also receives `$errorBag` for explicit `:error="$errorBag->first('email')"`
bindings.

## Form-level Callouts

[Callout](../components/callout.md) displays bag messages that belong to no
field:

| Attribute | Shows | Publishes nothing when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error-for="key"` | `MessageBag::first('key')` | the key has no message |
| `error-summary` | every key's first message, in bag order; a `firstlight::validation.summary` heading when there are two or more | the bag is empty |

Both default to `danger`, reject `message`, and are mutually exclusive. They
never receive field focus. The summary follows bag order, which is the order
of your rules, so list rules in screen order.

## Announcements and focus

| Interaction | Spoken once | Screen-reader focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@press` or `@submit` that adds messages | the summary of the whole bag | first invalid field in render order |
| any other event (model sync, `@change`, `updated{Property}`) that adds messages | only the messages it added | unchanged |
| an interaction that adds no message | nothing | unchanged |

"Adds messages" means a failed `validate()` or `validateOnly()`, or
`addError()`. Frames republished before the next interaction carry the same
alert, and the platforms act on it once. iOS moves
VoiceOver focus and posts an announcement. Android acts while TalkBack is on:
Text Field, Text Area, and Code Editor take input focus, and every field
announces.

## Participating fields

These components apply bag messages when the screen uses `ValidatesFields`:

[Text Field](../components/text-field.md),
[Text Area](../components/text-area.md),
[Checkbox](../components/checkbox.md),
[Switch](../components/switch.md),
[Select](../components/select.md),
[Segmented](../components/segmented.md),
[Choice Group](../components/choice-group.md),
[Pill Group](../components/pill-group.md),
[Date Picker](../components/date-picker.md),
[Time Picker](../components/time-picker.md),
[Slider](../components/slider.md),
and [Stepper](../components/stepper.md).

`required` on those fields is display metadata and does not run Laravel rules.

## Current limitations

- Only public instance properties are validated. Nested and wildcard rule keys
  are not supported.
- Call `validate()` and `validateOnly()` from actions and property hooks, not
  from `mount()` or `render()`. Those lifecycle methods still sit on
  NativePHP's generic `Throwable` overlay path, so a `ValidationException`
  paints the red overlay instead of field messages.
- `addError()` does not throw and may run from `render()` when a fixture needs
  a stable failed frame.

--- Source: docs/reference/screen-assertions.md ---

# Screen Assertions

`FirstlightUI\Testing\ScreenAssertions::register()` adds the methods below to
NativePHP's `Native\Mobile\Testing\TestableComponent`, the object returned by
`Native::test()` and `Native::visit()`. They read the most recently published
Element Tree. Interactions send the event type and callback id that the
Firstlight iOS and Android renderers send, then re-render the screen as the
harness does after `tap()` or `input()`.

NativePHP's own methods are unchanged and work on Firstlight controls. These
include `input()`, `tap()`, `toggle()`, `check()`, `set()`, `assertSee()`,
`assertSet()`, and `assertElement()`. For example, `input('email', ...)` types
into a Text Field bound with `native:model="email"`.

## Targets

A field target is either an element `ref` or the property name in the
element's `native:model` binding. A List row is identified by its exact
`headline`.

## Fields and validation

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `field($target)` | Returns the wire node for the target, or fails. |
| `assertFieldError($target, $message = null)` | The field's published `error` is not empty and, when given, equals `$message`. |
| `assertNoFieldError($target)` | The field's published `error` is empty. |
| `assertHasErrors($keys)` | The screen's `ValidatesFields` MessageBag has each key. `['email' => 'message']` also requires that message. |
| `assertHasNoErrors($keys = null)` | The bag is empty, or has none of the given keys. |
| `choose($target, $value)` | Chooses the option whose stable value equals `$value` (compared as a string) in a Select, Segmented, Pill Group, or Choice Group. Fails when no option has that value, or the option is disabled or cannot be chosen. A Select option that is already selected cannot be chosen. |

## Lists

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `listItem($headline)` | Returns the first List Item node with that headline, or fails and lists the headlines. |
| `assertListItem($headline, $matcher = null)` | A row exists. `$matcher` receives the wire node and must return `true`. |
| `assertMissingListItem($headline)` | No row has that headline. |
| `assertListItemCount($count)` | The tree contains exactly `$count` List Item rows. |
| `pressListItem($headline, $action = null)` | Presses the row, or the leading or trailing swipe action with the label `$action`. Fails for a disabled row. |

## Confirmation Dialog

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `assertConfirmationDialog($title = null)` | A Confirmation Dialog is visible, optionally with that title. |
| `assertNoConfirmationDialog()` | No Confirmation Dialog is visible. |
| `confirmDialog($title = null)` | Sends the visible dialog's `@press`. |
| `cancelDialog($title = null)` | Sends the visible dialog's `@dismiss`. |

## Feedback

Call `FirstlightUI\Facades\Feedback::fake()` before the screen sends Feedback.

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `assertFeedbackSent($message, $tone = null)` | Feedback with that message, and optionally that `FeedbackTone`, was sent. |
| `assertNoFeedbackSent()` | No Feedback was sent. |

## Pest expectations

`register()` also adds two expectations when Pest is loaded:

```php
expect(Native::test(SignupScreen::class))
    ->toHaveFieldError('email')
    ->toHaveListItem('Inbox');
```

They pair with NativePHP's `Native\Mobile\Testing\PestExpectations`.

## make:firstlight-screen

```bash
php artisan make:firstlight-screen {name} [--form] [--list] [--destroy] [--test] [--force]
```

| Option | Generates |
| --- | --- |
| none | `App\NativeComponents\{name}` extending `FirstlightUI\NativeComponent`, with `render()` returning `native.{kebab-name}`, and a Blade view with a title. |
| `--form` | A required `name` property, `$rules`, `save()` calling `submit()`, a Text Field bound with `native:model`, and a Save Button with `:loading="$submitting"`. |
| `--list` | `mount()`, `reload()`, `loadMore()`, `open()`, and a `listQuery()` stub. A List bound to `@refresh` and `@endReached` renders `$this->listItems`. |
| `--destroy` | Includes `--list`. Adds `requestDeletion()`, `cancelDeletion()`, and `deleteItem()`; rows disabled by `denies('delete', $item)`; a Delete swipe action; and a destructive Confirmation Dialog. |
| `--test` | `tests/Feature/NativeComponents/{name}Test.php` that uses `Native::test()` and these assertions. |
| `--force` | Overwrites existing files. Without it the command fails and writes nothing if any target exists. |

The command is registered only when the application runs in the console.

--- Source: docs/reference/compatibility.md ---

# Compatibility

| Dependency or platform | Current requirement |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `^8.4` |
| NativePHP Mobile | `^4.6` |
| NativePHP Mobile UI | `^0.8` |
| iOS application target | iOS 18.0 or later |
| Android application target | API 29 or later |
| Firstlight Swift package | iOS 18 or later |
| Swift tools | Swift 6.2 |

These are the package's current declared floors. Firstlight does not promise support for earlier versions. Both the iOS and Android renderers are required for a public component; the same documented EDGE example works on both platforms.

After changing NativePHP versions, run `composer update` and `php artisan native:install --force` so bundled PHP binaries, native project files, and plugin copies match the resolved release.

## Runtime response contract

### Supported response-revision contract

Extend `FirstlightUI\NativeComponent`, not the upstream EDGE base, for screens
using Firstlight controls, with NativePHP at the floors above.

The base stamps the **final chrome-wrapped root** with the integer prop
`firstlight_response_revision`. Its counter is private, process-wide, and
monotonically increasing across screen instances within the PHP process, not
component state to bind, persist, or set yourself. An otherwise unchanged full
response therefore differs from the previous frame and reaches the renderers.
The one exception is the final frame `back()` publishes before popping the
screen: it keeps the current revision, so an unchanged screen is not republished
mid-pop. On iOS such a frame would re-push the screen being left.

This deliberately bypasses whole-frame equality suppression for each completed
screen response. It trades that deduplication saving for reliable reconciliation
of unchanged values; publication cost still needs soak/performance qualification.

- Normal Blade paths are automatic: a global Laravel `View` returned from
  `render()`, `$this->view()`, and the inferred view all receive the revision.
- Programmatic Element roots must return `$this->response($element)` from
  `render()`. This adds normal screen chrome as well as the root revision.
  Use it only for raw Element content, not an already-completed `view()` or
  `fromView()` response. Custom `wrapWithChrome()` overrides must call the parent.
- Nested children are emitted untouched; partials are unstamped. Neither is an
  independent full response under this contract.
- `renderStreaming()` is final and returns `false`. Streaming bypasses this
  contract and cannot be opted into by a subclass.
- Existing concerns such as `ValidatesFields` remain usable separately, but
  adding a trait to the upstream base does not provide this publication contract.

The revision is **not a per-event acknowledgement**. It does not prevent
publication coalescing or serialize simultaneous proposals. Applications must
not infer that every event receives a separately observable response.
This is a screen-rendering contract, not a replacement for NativePHP's generic
publisher: framework-owned loading placeholders and error/dump overlays are
outside it.

### Upstream context and qualification

The October 2026 Android and iOS PHP 8.5.11 bundles still suppress byte-identical
frames in the shared C runtime. Android `treePublicationId`, shipped in Mobile
4.1.0 ([#280](https://github.com/NativePHP/mobile-air/pull/280)), only helps after
a publication reaches Kotlin. The cross-platform bug
[#365](https://github.com/NativePHP/mobile-air/issues/365) remains upstream;
the response revision makes Firstlight independent of it.

The permanent implementation was checked on October 19, 2026 with Mobile 4.6.0,
Mobile UI 0.8.0, and the official PHP 8.5.11 bundles: 14 nonstreaming phases each
on an Android emulator and iOS simulator. Each phase delivered three proposals
through a normal Blade screen using Firstlight's base, without app-authored
revision props. Repeated Switch/Pill rejection, Segmented rejection, validation,
accepted Switch changes, 500 ms rejection, and rapid same-control bursts passed.
Rapid bursts deliberately coalesce a second tap while pending; they do not
prove one response per physical tap. The earlier spike did not reproduce a
baseline Segmented failure, so these results do not establish a Segmented fix.

Package regression tests cover Blade, inferred views, hand-built responses,
remounts, nested children, and unstamped partials. This is not production
qualification. Firstlight 1.0.0 is a release candidate pending physical-device,
soak/performance, and wider app qualification, including simultaneous controls.
